subject: Re: Sovereign Health — residency crediting and HSM amortization options
messages:
From: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@sovereignethealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@sovereignethealth.com
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency credits + HSM amortization — initial questions

Karthik / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We pulled together a short list of follow-ups from procurement and infra regarding the compliance add-ons before we route this up to legal/finance:

- How do you typically credit on-prem / sovereign residency commitments against recurring compliance fees?
- For HSM: can Redwood provide an amortization option to offset our one-time HSM procurement (we would buy HSM appliances) against monthly "HSM seat" charges over a defined period? If so, what length windows do you support (24/36/48 months)?
- Audit log retention: can we get a blended rate if we commit to a 24-month residency in two EU regions?

Attached is a short questionnaire (Sovereign_Questions_v3.pdf) with the procurement team’s template. We need to show a few pricing scenarios to our CFO by 3/18. Can you turn around high-level scenarios (no PO required) that show: 1) HSM seat monthly pricing vs amortized capex credit over 36 months, and 2) residency credit against audit log fees for a 2-region commit.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Oliver
Oliver Hayes
Head of Cloud Procurement
Sovereignet Health


From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@sovereignethealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency credits + HSM amortization — initial questions

Oliver — thanks for the clear ask and the deadline. We can absolutely produce scenario-level pricing by 3/17 to give you time for CFO review. Quick notes up front:

- We support amortizing customer-owned HSM/Appliance capex as a credit against recurring HSM seat fees. Standard examples we use are 24/36/48 months; 36 months tends to be the clean midpoint for financial teams.
- Residency credits are usually structured as a percent rebate on audit-log and residency surcharge line items, tiered by commit size and duration.
- For a two-EU-region commit we can model both a blended and region-specific credit so you can see sensitivity.

Ben will attach a draft cost-model (spreadsheet) with 3 permutations; Laura will confirm whether we can include a one-time onboarding credit for scale projects. I’ll aim to get a preliminary PDF to you by EOD Wednesday.

If procurement wants a 30-minute slot Thursday morning to walk the numbers, we can do that.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@sovereignethealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Residency credits + HSM amortization — draft scenarios attached

Oliver / Karthik — putting the model in your hands. Attached: HSM_Cost_Model.xlsx. Summary of the three scenarios (top-line):

1) Seat-first: No capex credit. HSM seat = $3,200/mo per FIPS-backed slot. Audit log (30d retention) = $0.0025/GB/mo, residency surcharge 12% on storage/compute for EU regions.
2) Capex-offset 36m: We amortize customer HSM purchase at 36 months and credit up to 80% of amortized value against HSM seat fees (the other 20% covers ongoing maintenance/firmware support). With a $150k appliance, effective seat price falls to ~$1,800/mo for the committed seats.
3) Hybrid: 12-month onboarding credit (~$25k) + 24m amortization window with a 60% offset for capex credits and a reduced residency surcharge (9%) after commit is met.

Assumptions and caveats are in the first worksheet. I’ve flagged the cells you’ll want to stress-test.

Attachments: HSM_Cost_Model.xlsx (cost model)

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@sovereignethealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency credits + HSM amortization — draft scenarios attached

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of asks from procurement/finance:

- Can you produce the capex amortization math so it’s an explicit line on our monthly invoice (we need auditability for our auditors).
- Instead of an 80% cap on credit, would Redwood consider a straight amortization credit equal to 100% of the amortized capex over 36 months provided we sign a minimum 36-month residency/throughput commit and pre-pay the first 6 months? That materially reduces our TCO and makes the commercial decision easier.
- For audit logs/retention: can you show a 24mo retention tier with a blended price when spread across two EU regions (we will likely split 60/40 primary/secondary).

Lastly, does Redwood have any precedents where the HSM vendor warranty/maintenance fees are treated separately (i.e., we continue to pay the vendor but Redwood offsets the recurring product charge)? That’s our preferred accounting treatment.

Maya
Procurement Manager
Sovereignet Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@sovereignethealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency credits + HSM amortization — draft scenarios attached

Maya — quick reply on the three asks and our recommended path so we can get toward a commercial terms doc: 

1) Invoice-level amortization line: yes, we can expose a discrete "HSM capex credit" line on the monthly invoice. That line will mirror the amortization schedule (we typically run amortization as a straight-line credit over the agreed window). We will add a reconciliation appendix for auditors.

2) 100% amortization in exchange for 36m commit + 6m prepay: we can do that but we’ll request a short list of protective guardrails: a) a clawback window (pro-rata) if residency or committed throughput is materially breached, b) a one-time integration onboarding fee to cover our HW integration effort (we model this at $22k but open to negotiation), and c) the HSM vendor maintenance (warranty) should remain with the customer — we will not credit vendor maintenance, only Redwood product charges.

3) Audit log blended 24mo pricing: we’ll produce a blended example (60/40 split) and include the tiered residency discount.

Next steps: We’ll update the spreadsheet with the 100% amortization scenario + invoice line and turn around a one-page commercial principles doc by EOD Monday. If that is acceptable, I’ll also draft a short amendment template for legal with the clawback language.

Laura Bennett
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@sovereignethealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency credits + HSM amortization — draft scenarios attached

Thanks everyone — that path sounds workable. Two quick confirmations before we escalate internally: 

1) We agree to 36-month residency commit + 6-month prepay in exchange for the 100% straight-line amortization credit (subject to the clawback terms you mentioned).
2) We understand vendor HSM maintenance remains our responsibility — Redwood will credit only Redwood recurring product charges.

If you can send the one-page commercial principles and the spreadsheet with the invoice-line added, we'll present to finance next Tuesday (3/20). Please email a DocuSign-ready amendment if legal says they want formal sign-off after finance review.

Oliver
Head of Cloud Procurement | Sovereignet Health
